name: In-Line Dimmer Module

steps.text: If you will configure the dimmer with software, write down its Insteon ID and the fixture it is installed in.
Turn off the circuit breaker or fuse supplying power to the fixture. Check that the power is off by toggling the load from its local switch.
Remove the wall plate from the fixture, unscrew it and remove it from the junction box.
Disconnect the wires from the fixture. If they can't be unscrewed, cut them and strip 1/2 inch of insulation off the ends. Make sure the wires aren't touching anything.
Turn on the circuit breaker, use a voltage meter to identify the line, load, neutral and ground wires, then turn the breaker off again.
Using the included wire nuts, connect the dimmer's bare copper wire to ground, white to neutral, red to load and black to line.
Turn power back on at the circuit breaker or fuse panel.
Use the dimmer's On and Off buttons to test the installation.
steps.expect: The load turns on and off.

steps.text: Set the local on-level and ramp rate for the connected load.
Link the dimmer to an Insteon controller.
Gently place the dimmer into the junction box, making sure nothing can accidentally press the buttons on its face.
Reinstall the fixture.

notes: Link the dimmer before you finish installing the fixture, while its buttons are still reachable.

steps.text: With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the SET button until the dimmer double-beeps.
steps.expect: double beep; status LED flashes once, then turns on if the load is off or off if the load is on

notes: The dimmer links only as a responder. First put the controller in linking mode; for most controllers, press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds or the On or scene button for 10 seconds. The controller stays in linking mode for 4 minutes.
Pressing and holding the dimmer's SET button starts linking mode.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
With the controller in linking mode, press and hold the SET button until the dimmer double-beeps.
steps.expect: double beep; status LED flashes once, then turns on if the load is off or off if the load is on

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder; the device makes no link back to the Hub.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: With the controller in unlinking mode, press and hold the SET button until the dimmer double-beeps.
steps.expect: double beep; status LED flashes once, then turns on if the load is off or off if the load is on

notes: First put the controller in unlinking mode; for most controllers, press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds twice or the On or scene button for 10 seconds twice. The controller stays in unlinking mode for 4 minutes.

steps.text: Make sure the dimmer is unlinked from all controllers.
Turn off the breaker supplying power to the dimmer's fixture.
Wait 10 seconds.
Push in the SET button and hold it while a partner turns the circuit breaker back on.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: After a few seconds the dimmer double-beeps and the load turns on.

steps.text: Unlink the dimmer from every controller it was linked to.
Stop using the dimmer.

notes: Otherwise the controllers retry commands and cause network delays.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Linked by holding SET for 10 seconds.
